situation:
You are the marketing director of CLEARSPACE HOME ORGANIZATION, a firm that sorts, sizes and installs storage in clients' homes. The owner (judge) started the firm eleven years ago and still meets every new client personally. The owner (judge) has asked you to recommend how the firm should answer a competitor that has taken work away from it over the last two quarters.

That competitor, NEATWORKS, opened locally last spring and prices a standard closet project a third below what CLEARSPACE HOME ORGANIZATION charges. Because the firm sells a service rather than a product, what a client buys is the day itself: the organizers who arrive on time and the calm, unhurried handover at the end. Bookings from repeat clients have fallen for the first time.

The owner (judge) has already deferred three months of their own pay so the firm can cut the price of its recurring package to match NEATWORKS this quarter and hold its share. Cutting the price that way teaches clients to expect the lower price next year, and it leaves the owner (judge) without income going into a quarter that will earn less on every job.

The other course is to hold the price and sign a contract offered by a vacation rental management company to reset and restock forty rental properties between guest stays. That contract guarantees volume through the summer, but it would tie up two of the firm's five organizers in the season when home bookings peak, and rushed handovers would damage the reputation for unhurried service the firm's price rests on.

The owner (judge) wants you to explain how the firm is positioned against NEATWORKS, weigh the risk in each course, and recommend one of them. The owner (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and after you have presented and answered questions, the owner (judge) will thank you for your time.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the owner (judge) of CLEARSPACE HOME ORGANIZATION. Business background is the same as the situation above. You have asked your marketing director to tell you how the firm is positioned against NEATWORKS now that a lower-priced competitor is in town, to weigh what each course of action risks, and to recommend either cutting the price of the recurring package this quarter or holding the price and signing the vacation rental management company's contract.

You will greet the participant and ask to hear their ideas. After the participant has presented, ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: How would you explain this to the organizers it affects most?
What would you tell them about the pay you deferred?
